description: Base 4 (builds on Base 3 / old 3.3, voice-3b311f32, folder v303_generalist_inplane; carries Gripper 21 and Handle 7, voice-448df859, handle height ~12 mm to match the finger via the shared handle_over param): Simplify again: there are too many pieces. Focus especially on how the base links to the handle; that connection has too many parts. Cut the part count wherever possible. Baseline to beat (Base 3 README/exports): 9 separate parts = 8 printed (2 fingers, 2 handles, 2 side gears, 1 pinion, 1 base) + the RS00, plus 12 M3 screws (6 flange through the pinion, 6 front ring) = 21 pieces total. Handle-to-gear link today: each handle's tail band wraps the finger's base hook and a key sticks down from it; that sits in a cradle cut into the side gear's hub (with a key notch), the gear's web reaches the pivot, and the gear's axle turns in a plain bushing in the base; the pinion on the RS00 flange drives the right gear, which meshes the left. So finger -> handle (tail+key) -> gear cradle -> gear axle -> base bushing, and the pinion is a separate part from the gears. Beat both counts (e.g. merge handle into gear or pinion into the flange, fewer screws) and say the new count in VERSIONS.txt. Keep it parameterized (params.json + Tune sliders), driven by the single RS00, with the strap slots clear. New folder, params.json-first per AGENTS.md; name it Base 4 in VERSIONS.txt / catalog.

results.identified_issue: Merged handle_body() into gear(): gear = difference(union(gear_solid, handle_body), finger_pocket) where finger_pocket is offset(fit) of the finger profile above web_y1. A first try cut the hub pocket tail_gap off and unioned the handle separately; the coincident faces made the assembled-pose meshes non-watertight, hence the single cut. stop_depth/stop_width and key_* params removed; handle_over 0. Screw reduction via motor_out_screws / motor_front_screws (ring() uses them; motor model keeps all 6 holes; asserts that screws divide holes). Rejected: dropping the pinion by putting the motor coaxial with the right pivot (reverses Jake's Base 3 'single motor centered' ask). Handle-gear parts are named 'Right gear'/'Left gear' so gallery.js's HANDLE regex classifies them as Base. Unverified: print orientation, finger retention in +y, bolt strength in plastic.
results.summary: Base 4: each handle and its gear are now one print, and the motor joints use 3 bolts instead of 6. That's 13 pieces, down from Base 3's 21.
results.detailed_description:
Base 4 is in v304_generalist_one_piece_drive and listed as Base 4 in VERSIONS.txt and the catalog. It carries Gripper 21 and Handle 7.

The handle-to-base link was the worst part, so I merged the handle into its side gear. The handle's tail now runs straight into the gear hub, so the key, the key notch and the cradle are gone. The finger drops into the handle-gear from the dorsal side: its hook goes between the handle's feet and its base corner into a pocket in the hub. It sits on the gear's web, and the web now does the stop strip's job, so the strip is gone too. The handle is exactly the finger's 12 mm edge-on (Handle 7 height). The chain went from finger > handle > key > cradle > gear axle > bushing to finger > handle-gear > bushing.

Screws: the pinion now bolts through every other hole of the RS00's 6-hole flange (3 M3), and the base plate uses every other front-ring hole (3 M3). The two dowels still locate it. My shear estimate is about 350 N per bolt at the 14 N·m peak. That's a calculation only, not a test. Two new sliders, motor_out_screws and motor_front_screws, put either joint back to 6.

Count: 6 printed parts (2 fingers, 2 handle-gears, pinion, base) + the RS00 + 6 M3 = 13 pieces. Base 3 had 8 + 1 + 12 = 21. I kept the motor centred with its pinion, as you asked in Base 3. The only way to lose the pinion is to put the motor under the right finger again (Base 1/2 style), which would make it 12 pieces. Say if you want that.

All 32 geometry checks pass. New ones: the finger drops in without touching, rests on the web, gets driven both ways (turned 1° either way, the gear hits it), and each handle-gear prints as one solid. The strap-tunnel keep-outs stay clear from 0 to 30°. Nothing printed.

Caveats: only friction keeps the finger from lifting out of its handle-gear (+y), as in Base 3. The handle-gear is a bigger print with overhangs (the teeth start 2 mm above the web), and I haven't worked out print orientation. In the preview's mix-and-match, the handle-gears count as Base parts, so picking another Handle with Base 4 draws that handle over the built-in one.

summary: Base 4 must simplify Base 3's gripper assembly, especially the finger-handle-gear-base linkage, which currently totals 21 pieces including 8 printed parts and 12 screws. Cut both the part count and screw count below that baseline, record the new count in VERSIONS.txt, and keep it parameterized and driven by the single RS00.
